(‘The Group’) is pleased to

and transparent account of the 
Group's financial and non-financial 
performance, highlighting how it 
creates sustainable value for all 
stakeholders. Prepared in accordance 
with the Securities and Exchange 
Board of India (Listing Obligations 
and Disclosure Requirements - 
LODR) 2015, it presents the Group's 
strategic priorities, operating 
environment, governance framework, 
risks, opportunities and performance 
during the year.

Reinventing Capabilities. 
Accelerating Growth.
When the environment changes, the ability to 
evolve becomes a competitive advantage.
Markets shift. Customer expectations 
change. Technology redraws possibilities. 
Regulation creates new openings. In such 
an environment, growth is no longer simply 
about doing more of what has worked. It is 
about continuously renewing the capabilities 
that make new growth possible.
FY 2025-26 was a year of that renewal for 
Thomas Cook India.
Across the organisation, capabilities were 
being reimagined, from technology and 
digital platforms to distribution, partnerships, 
customer engagement and financial 
services. The Group responded to changing 
market dynamics by finding new avenues 
for growth, entering emerging opportunity 
spaces, sharpening its portfolio and creating 
more focused platforms for the future.
What connects these developments is 
not any single initiative, but a mindset: to 
question what can be done differently, adapt 
with purpose, build the capabilities to act 
on new possibilities, and turn them into 
lasting advantage. Because in a changing 
environment, the ability to evolve is not just a 
response to change — it is what creates the 
next opportunity for growth. 
Reinventing Capabilities. 
Accelerating Growth.
Because growth is not only about 
finding the next opportunity. It is about 
becoming capable of creating one.

Company Snapshot
For more than 145 years, Thomas Cook (India) 
Limited ('TCIL', 'The Group') has been at the centre 
of this ecosystem, building one of India's leading 
integrated travel and travel-related financial 
services enterprises.
Through market-leading businesses spanning 
travel, foreign exchange, payment solutions, 
destination management, hospitality, travel 
technology and digital imaging, we simplify cross-
border mobility for leisure travellers, corporates, 
students, institutions and financial partners alike.In an increasingly connected world, the 
movement of people, money and experiences 
has become deeply interconnected.

Our strength lies not in the breadth of 
our portfolio alone, but in the way our 
businesses complement one another. 
Built around a portfolio of 16 leading B2C 
and B2B brands, we have developed an 
ecosystem designed to serve.
From our market-leading Foreign 
Exchange business, we provide a 
comprehensive range of services 
that enable seamless cross-border 
transactions for individual travellers, 
students, corporates and institutions. 
Alongside this, Leisure Holidays offer 
end-to-end holiday offerings for 
Indian travellers across domestic and 
international destinations, delivering 
trusted and personalised travel 
experiences at scale.
Our MICE (Meetings, Incentives, 
Conferences & Events) business provides 
end-to-end corporate event and group 
travel solutions for clients across 
India and global markets, ensuring 
seamless execution and strong on-
ground coordination. Our Destination 
Management Group operates across a strong network, supported by global 
partners, delivering deep local expertise 
and reliable service delivery.
Our Corporate Travel business 
provides integrated travel management 
solutions for enterprises, supported 
by digital platforms, data-driven 
tools and strong service capabilities 
that enhance efficiency and traveller 
experience. Complementing these are 
Sterling Holiday Resorts in hospitality, 
offering curated leisure stays and 
experiences, and DEI Holdings in 
technology-enabled imaging, which 
enhances visitor engagement at global 
attractions. Each of these businesses 
operates independently while collectively 
strengthening the broader ecosystem 
and expanding the value we deliver to 
customers.
This integrated model allows the Group 
to participate across multiple segments 
of travel and financial services while 
delivering a seamless experience for 
every customer.TCIL’s diversified business model 
opens several avenues for growth while 
strengthening resilience across market 
cycles.
Backed by the long-term stewardship of 
the Fairfax Group, industry-leading CRISIL 
AA/Stable and CRISIL A1+ credit ratings 
on the bank facilities, corporate credit 
rating and commercial paper programme 
of Thomas Cook (India) Limited (TCIL) 
and a steady focus on customer trust, 
we continue to invest in innovation, 
operational strength and the capabilities 
that keep us ready for the future.Enterprise Built on 
Complementary Strengths
Headquartered in India, TCIL has 
built one of the largest travel service 
networks in the Asia-Pacific region, 
with operations across 28 countries 
and 5 continents.
Our omnichannel platform pairs a 
wide physical presence with digital 
capabilities, so customers can reach 
us through whichever channel they 
prefer. Backed by technology, AI-led 
customer engagement and deep 
domain expertise, we continue to 
raise the standard of convenience, 
accessibility and personalisation 
across the customer experiences.Scale that 
Extends beyond

A Portfolio 
Built around 
Customer ValueChanging geopolitical landscape   Reinventing in a dynamic environment
FY 2025-26 brought a significant shift in the travel environment, with geopolitical developments, changing travel patterns, 
currency movements, weather events and evolving customer behaviour reshaping demand across markets. Rather than relying 
on a conventional operating playbook, we responded by adapting our products, expanding customer propositions, using our 
diversified portfolio more actively and accelerating technology adoption.
Travellers are increasingly embracing digital-first journeys, for more convenience, flexibility, personalisation, and seamless 
experiences. 
Building on our existing tech-powered, omnichannel ecosystem, we continued to enhance digital offerings across Forex (TC 
Pay App, WhatsApp, website, FX Mate), Leisure (AI Chat Bot, Voice Bot, AI Agent Assist, Website) and Corporate Travel (Online 
Booking Tool). Digital adoption continues to grow at 21.2% in Forex and 20% in Leisure, and 53% touchless transactions in 
Corporate Travel. We are further leveraging AI to enhance personalisation, customer experience and operational efficiency.Financial Services
The travel component of the Liberalised Remittance Scheme 
(LRS) declined by 6%, while education contracted by ~22% to 
25%. Against this backdrop, our retail portfolio grew its education 
and travel categories by 17% and 13%, respectively, supported by 
enhanced customer segmentation and expanded omni-channel 
distribution including our partnership with Blinkit expanded 
access to forex cards through instant delivery.
We also strengthened our proposition through the Zero Markup 
Forex Card and an expanded multi-currency prepaid card portfolio, 
offering customers exchange rates certainty ahead of travel.  Travel
Rupee depreciation and heightened tensions in the Middle 
East altered the dynamics and connectivity of international 
travel, particularly long-haul.
Conflict-driven fuel price volatility added to cost pressures. 
Against this backdrop, we responded by leveraging our 
diversified portfolio, shifting focus towards resilient short-
haul and domestic demand. We also recalibrated our holiday 
portfolio to respond to changing dynamics with increasing 
focus on destinations like China, Vietnam and Japan.Excessive rainfall and landslides impacted Northern India, affecting ~40% of Northern India inventory and occupancy at newly 
added resorts in Q2 FY 2025-26.
Sterling responded by redirecting demand towards properties across the South, West and East, while using this period to 
accelerate expansion. Internal resources were redeployed towards the launch of seven new resorts in a single quarter. Rebalancing the leisure hospitality portfolio Shifting travel dynamics  
Optimizing the product portfolio Changing landscape of travel   
Accelerating digital adoption Evolving travel behaviour  The escalation of the US-Iran-Israel conflict disrupted aviation routes, fuel supply chains and travel sentiment, particularly across 
westbound routes and the Middle East. The Pahalgam attack, operation Sindoor, Protests in Nepal and travel advisories during 
the India-Pakistan border conflict further affected traveller’s confidence and travel flows. The impact varied across businesses, 
with Digital Imaging and Desert Adventures particularly exposed to the Middle East.
We responded by strengthening customer assurance and flexibility through: 
TravSure: Offering free rescheduling and refunds for war-like disruptions, along with emergency hotel stays.
Visa Rejection Cover: Providing financial protection and flexibility to travellers in case of visa rejection. Expanding customer assurance

Dear Shareholders,
It is my privilege to address you for the 
first time, as the Chairman of the Board 
of Thomas Cook (India) Limited. 
Before I address my shareholders, I 
want to take a moment to reflect on a 
transition for our corporate family. After 
a truly illustrious 25-year tenure, Mr. 
Madhavan Menon stepped down from 
his executive duties and retired from 
the Board in September 2025. Under his 
visionary guidance, Thomas Cook India 
transformed from a traditional travel 
operator into the dynamic travel and 
financial services conglomerate we are 
today. We owe him a tremendous debt of 
gratitude for this legacy.
As the Group enters its next phase, we 
remain focused on building on the strong 
foundations established over the years 
and advancing our strategic priorities further weighed on travel sentiment 
and consumer confidence. As our 
teams started to drive recovery, the 
latter half of the year witnessed the 
start of the Israel-United States-
Iran conflict in February 2026 that 
continues as we speak. This regional 
conflict impacted one of the busiest air 
and shipping corridors and completely 
disrupted westbound flight corridors. 
If that were not enough, driven by the 
instability and oil imports, etc, the 
Indian Rupee faced intense volatility, 
depreciating more than 10% in a single 
year. These compounding factors 
inevitably cascaded into the broader 
economy, significantly inflating airfare 
and all aspects of travel costs, which 
in turn dampened outbound travel 
momentum while domestic travel was 
further compounded by fuel and LPG 
shortages across hotels and other 
travel intermediaries. 
Despite these challenges, the Group 
remained agile and responsive, 
navigating the disruptions while 
continuing to support our customers 
and maintain business continuity.The Power of a Diversified 
Foundation
The year demonstrated the strength 
and resilience of our diversified 
business model, with our businesses 
continuing to capture opportunities 
across markets despite a dynamic 
operating environment. The first nine 
months of FY 2025-26 saw healthy 
travel demand, with Total Consolidated 
Income growing 7% and EBITDA 
improving marginally. This momentum 
was moderated in the final quarter, as 
geopolitical developments, particularly 
in the Middle East, and shorter selling 
windows affected performance. Group 
revenue in Q4 FY 2025-26 stood at 
` 17,707 mn, a decline of 10% over the 
corresponding period last year.
Despite the Q4 impact, Total 
Consolidated Income grew 3.3% 
to `  85,578 mn for the full year. 
Consolidated Profit Before Tax, before 
exceptional items, stood at ` 3,328 mn, 
compared with `  3,852 mn in the 
previous fiscal year. At the standalone 
level, Profit Before Tax grew 2% to 
` 1,690 mn, reflecting the resilience of 
our core India operations.disruptions, India continues to shine 
as one of the fastest growing large 
economies, clocking a remarkable 7.7% 
real GDP growth for FY 2025-26.
Navigating Geopolitical Volatility 
FY 2025-26 has been a year of extreme 
unpredictability, which our Company 
navigated with resilience, reinvention, 
and agility. Our ability to adapt, innovate, 
and stay focused has enabled us to 
emerge stronger and better positioned 
to capture the opportunities ahead. 
The year commenced under the heavy 
shadow of the tragic Pahalgam terrorist 
attack in April 2025, which necessitated 
heightened security protocols and 
travel restrictions, followed by 
Operation Sindoor and significant 
airspace disruptions. These events 
had an immediate impact on domestic 
and outbound travel sentiment during 
the critical summer booking season. 
While a series of timely interventions 
helped stabilise operations and restore 
traveller confidence by early May, the 
recovery was subsequently tempered 
by the tragic Air India crash, which with confidence. Our succession 
planning is anchored in continuity, 
experience and a deep understanding 
of our businesses. In this context, the 
appointment of Mr. Mahesh Iyer as 
Managing Director & Chief Executive 
Officer reflects a natural progression 
of leadership within the Group. With 
over three decades of experience with 
the Company, Mr. Iyer has held a wide 
range of leadership positions across 
the organisation, including Head of 
Foreign Exchange, Chief Operating 
Officer, Chief Executive Officer and 
Executive Director, before assuming his 
current role.
The Board has full confidence in Mr. 
Iyer and his executive team to build 
on this strong institutional knowledge, 
execute our strategy and lead the Group 
through its next phase of development. Chairman’s Message
Reinventing the Road Ahead
As the Group enters its 
next phase, we remain 
focused on building on 
the strong foundations 
established over the 
years and advancing 
our strategic priorities 
with confidence.
This continuity is further supported 
by the enduring backing of Fairfax 
Financial Holdings, providing a strong 
institutional foundation and a long-term 
perspective as we pursue sustainable 
value creation for all our stakeholders.
India’s strong macroeconomic 
fundamentals continue to reinforce 
our confidence in the potential of the 
travel and tourism sector. A favourable 
demographic dividend, aided by a 
rapidly expanding middle class with 
an aspiration to travel, along with 
supportive policy initiatives including 
the reduction in TCS rates, easing visa 
requirements, the growing strength 
of the Indian passport, and sustained 
investments in infrastructure – are 
collectively creating a runway for the 
industry’s next phase of growth and it 
is incredibly encouraging that despite 
the geo political headwinds and

The diversity of our portfolio was a 
key strength throughout the year. Our 
Financial Services business emerged 
as a significant stabiliser, delivering 
16% growth in retail turnover, supported 
by resilient demand across segments, 
including overseas education. Our 
Leisure Hospitality business to benefit 
from the strong preference for domestic 
travel, delivering 6.6% growth in full-year 
revenue.
Our geographic diversification also to 
strengthen the Group’s resilience. Within 
Travel & Related Services, underlying 
momentum remained encouraging 
despite evolving travel patterns and 
geopolitical disruptions, with income 
from operations growing 3.6%. This 
performance reflects the sustained 
appetite for travel and the strength of 
our operating platform.
Our Digital Imaging Solutions (DEI) and 
Desert Adventures DMS businesses 
saw moderation as developments in the 
Middle East impacted their respective 
markets. Both businesses, however, to 
strengthen operational efficiencies and 
remain well positioned to benefit as 
market conditions normalise.The year reinforced an important 
strength of our Group: the ability to 
leverage the breadth of our portfolio, 
geographic presence and diverse 
demand drivers to navigate changing 
conditions while continuing to create 
opportunities for sustainable growth.
AI Initiatives 
Artificial Intelligence is ushering in a 
fundamental shift in the global travel 
ecosystem. As customers increasingly 
rely on intelligent digital assistants to 
research, compare and plan journeys, 
AI is reshaping customer expectations 
while redefining how travel companies 
engage, personalise and create value. 
We believe this transformation will 
determine how effectively businesses 
anticipate customer needs, unlock 
new revenue opportunities and build 
enduring competitive advantage.
Recognising this structural shift, 
we  continued to accelerate our digital 
transformation by embedding AI 
and technology across customer 
and business journeys. Alongside 
strengthening our digital platforms and 
data capabilities, we remain focused on combining the power of AI with the trust, 
expertise and personalised service that 
define our business. This integrated 
phygital approach enables us to deliver 
superior customer experiences, drive 
operational excellence, and expand our 
reach across India’s rapidly evolving 
travel landscape.
Creating Value beyond Business
We remain steadfast in our 
commitment to Environmental, Social, 
and Governance (ESG) principles. As 
detailed in our Business Responsibility 
and Sustainability Report, we continue 
to foster an inclusive, merit-based 
workplace guided by our Equal 
Opportunity Policy, while advancing 
environmentally responsible practices 
across our operations and physical 
asset portfolio to minimise our 
environmental footprint. By embedding 
responsible business practices into our 
strategy and operations, we continue 
to create sustainable value for all our 
stakeholders.
Our commitment to creating lasting 
value extends well beyond business 
performance. Through the Fairfax India Charitable Foundation, Project 
Dialysis continues to expand access 
to affordable dialysis care across India, 
having delivered over 3.73 mn free 
dialysis sessions. During the year, the 
Fairfax India Charitable Foundation 
also broadened its scope to include 
vocational education, reflecting our 
belief that empowering communities 
requires both better healthcare and 
sustainable livelihood opportunities.
Ensuring Agility and Capital 
Discipline
In a world where volatility has become 
the norm, agility and financial discipline 
remain at the core of our strategy. 
We are continuously strengthening 
our ability to anticipate and adapt to 
geopolitical shifts, evolving traveller 
preferences, and market disruptions 
by rapidly identifying emerging 
opportunities, developing alternative 
travel destinations, and leveraging 
technology and innovation.
This adaptability is supported by a 
strong and disciplined balance sheet. 
As of March 31, 2026, we maintained 
Cash and Short Term Investments 
at `  26 bn, providing the liquidity and financial flexibility to navigate an 
uncertain global environment while 
continuing to invest in strategic growth 
opportunities. This balance between 
operational responsiveness and prudent 
capital allocation enables us to remain 
resilient, seize emerging opportunities, 
and create long-term value.
Acknowledgments
I want to extend my warmest gratitude 
to you, our shareholders, as well as 
the Central and State Governments,

Managing Director & CEO’s Message
Dear Shareholders,
Warm greetings to you all.
At Thomas Cook India, we believe that 
staying ahead demands continuous 
reinvention. To us, Reinvention is not 
simply about adapting to change; it is about 
anticipating it, embracing innovation, and 
creating new ways to deliver greater value 
for our customers. This belief has enabled 
us to evolve alongside our customers’ 
needs for over 145 years, while building an 
organisation that is more agile, resilient, 
and future-ready.
FY 2025-26 reinforced a fundamental 
truth: the human desire to explore, connect, 
and transact globally is unstoppable. 
While macro environments and travel 
patterns naturally evolve, the enthusiasm the fourth quarter. The first nine months of  
FY 2025-26 were characterised by 
relatively stable operating conditions 
and travel demand trends. During this 
period, the Group delivered a 7% increase 
in revenue, while EBITDA also improved 
marginally. The fourth quarter, however, 
reflected a markedly different operating 
environment, as geopolitical and 
macroeconomic developments became 
significantly more visible across the travel 
industry. Group revenue in Q4 FY 2025-26 
stood at ` 17,707 mn, a 10% decline over the 
corresponding period last year, reflecting 
the combined impact of the Middle East 
overhang, cost headwinds and a travel 
market recalibrating in real time. This 
resulted in an overall growth of 3.3% for   
FY 2025-26.
The impact of geopolitical disruptions 
was therefore concentrated rather than 
broad-based, with the greatest pressure 
felt by Desert Adventures in the Middle 
East and the UAE business of DEI, while 
several other segments continued to 
deliver growth. This is where the strength 
of our diversified model proved its value—
absorbing concentrated disruptions while 
allowing the broader portfolio to continue 
progressing.
We also strengthened our customer 
proposition to address emerging concerns 
across the travel journey.
TravSure, an industry-first travel 
assurance programme, addressed 
key travel disruptions typically 
excluded from conventional travel 
insurance, including war and war-like 
conditions, airspace closures and 
the need for 24x7 support. A first-of-
its-kind Visa Rejection Cover further 
gave travellers greater confidence 
and flexibility when planning their 
journeys.As geopolitical tensions escalated across 
the Middle East later in the year, customer 
safety and well-being remained our 
priority. From the first days of the West 
Asia conflict, we ensured that stranded 
passengers in the region were supported 
and brought home safely. We continued 
to keep travellers informed, support 
them through changing circumstances 
and offer flexible alternatives to those 
who chose to alter their travel plans. 
Responding effectively required agility 
and collaboration across our global 
network, reinforcing a customer-focused 
culture where people always come 
before process.
Customer trust and confidence are 
built not only through our response 
during difficult times, but also through 
everyday experiences. During the 
year, we simplified internal workflows, 
accelerated turnaround times, 
strengthened grievance resolution and 
continued investing in tools that enable 
our frontline teams to respond faster and 
with greater ownership. Together, these 
initiatives have made your Company’s 
experience more seamless, responsive 
and reassuring.
Travel and Travel Related Services 
Following the Customer, Not the Market
Another important lesson from the 
current times was that demand had not 
weakened; it had evolved. 
B2C Portfolio
Travellers became more selective about 
where and how they travelled. Shorter 
booking windows, easier visa access 
and a preference for destinations offering 
greater certainty shaped decisions 
far more than in the past. Rather than 
waiting for these trends to settle, we 
moved early to reshape our portfolio. This 
translated into strong momentum across 
our short-haul travel, which delivered 
17% growth, while demand for long-haul 
travel remained resilient despite elevated 
airfares, constrained airline capacity and 
longer visa processing timelines. India’s Travel Opportunity: Built on 
Strong Fundamentals
India’s Travel & Tourism opportunity 
is underpinned by structural tailwinds. 
A young and increasingly aspirational 
population, rising incomes, expanding 
middle-class households and rapid 
urbanisation are steadily broadening the 
consumer base for travel. 
Long-term projections indicate that 
India could add around 140 mn middle-
income households by 2030, alongside 
a significant expansion of the high-
income segment. The country’s young 
demographic profile continues to 
expand its working-age population and 
earning potential. This is translating 
into a greater propensity to spend on 
experiences, with travel increasingly 
moving from an occasional discretionary 
purchase to an important part of lifestyle 
and consumption. The expanding pool 
of Indians with access to international 
travel is another important indicator of 
this opportunity, with more than 143 
million passports issued cumulatively 
between March 2014 and March 2026, 
including over 1.38 mn passports issued 
in FY 2025-26 alone. This growing 
base of passport issuance reflects the 
increasing potential for outbound travel 
as Indian consumers become more 
globally connected and aspirational.
Putting Customer Confidence at the 
Centre
The year clarified what is within our 
control and what is not. While geopolitical 
events, airspace closures, exchange rate 
movements and negative news headlines 
remained outside our control, we chose 
to focus on what we could influence - 
allocating capital wisely, prioritising the 
right customers and markets, remaining 
invested in technology, making prudent 
investments and maintaining disciplined 
cost management.
It is important, therefore, to view our FY 
2025-26 performance through across two 
distinct periods: the first nine months and disciplined execution and customer-first 
focus enabled us to deliver ` 85,578 mn 
in total income, representing a 3.3% year-
on-year growth.
This performance is the direct result of 
placing customer-obsession at the heart 
of our growth strategy. We recognised 
that to truly remove friction from travel, 
we had to surround the customer with 
an ecosystem built entirely for their 
convenience. This meant designing 
targeted products that anticipate 
specific traveller needs, forging strategic 
partnerships that embed our services 
seamlessly into their everyday lives 
with technology and AI to ensure every 
interaction is simple to use, intuitive, real-
time, and deeply personalised.Reinventing Every Journey -

of our diversified portfolio, with growth 
across short-haul, domestic, Corporate

sustain momentum across the business.

At the same time, we expanded our reach 
through strategic partnerships. Our 
long-term alliance with Atlys embedded 
forex into the digital visa journey, while 
Muthoot Forex made our cards available 
across more than 7,000 branches 
nationwide. With Blinkit, we became 
India’s first provider to deliver forex cards 
to the doorstep within minutes, taking the 
service live across 12 cities. 
Additionally, TC Pay (our integrated FX 
services app) and FX on WhatsApp have 
emerged as important pillars of our 
digital-first distribution strategy, enabling 
customers to access forex services 
with greater speed and convenience. 
Transactions through TC Pay grew more 
than three-fold during the year, while forex 
transactions through WhatsApp increased 
2.6 times and website transactions 
grew by 8%, demonstrating the growing 
adoption of our digital sales & service 
channels. 
Thus, by turning a traditional service 
into a highly digital ecosystem, our retail 
forex business achieved a 21.2% digital 
penetration rate and maintained its market 
leadership, commanding nearly one-third 
of India’s prepaid forex card market.
In parallel, we complemented our digital 
expansion to strengthen our physical 
distribution network. Our extensive 
footprint of 130+ branches, 3,100+ 
partners and 17 airport counters ensure 
that customers can access our forex 
services wherever and whenever they 
need them. By seamlessly connecting 
our digital platforms, partner ecosystem 
and physical network, we are creating 
an increasingly integrated omnichannel 
experience - combining the convenience 
of digital with the trust and accessibility of 
our nationwide retail presence.
The impact of these initiatives was 
reflected in our financial performance, 
with overall turnover growing 8% during 
the year, revenue remaining stable and 
EBIT margins sustaining at a healthy 46%. The combination of digital adoption, 
an expanding distribution ecosystem 
and disciplined execution enabled the 
business to maintain profitability and 
strengthen its market position despite 
softer industry demand. 
Together, these investments in our digital 
and physical distribution capabilities 
enabled the business to continue gaining 
market share and expanding margins 
despite a challenging market environment. 
The RBI’s approval permitting Authorised

avenues for growth. We intend to leverage 
this opportunity to extend our trade-
related services building on our strong 
base of existing corporate relationships. 
Leisure Hospitality and Resorts
Growing from Strength to Strength
Sterling Holiday Resorts had a strong 
year, with its focused hospitality strategy 
translating into sustained growth and 
profitability. The business reported 7% 
growth in topline with EBIT margins 
at 24%. Now a pure-play hospitality 
business, Sterling is well positioned to 
capture the growing domestic travel 
opportunity: resort revenues grew 13%, 
room revenues 21%, and the business 
recorded its 25th consecutive profitable 
quarter, reflecting sustained momentum 
and operational strength.
Sterling closed the year operating 78 
resorts and more than 3,800 rooms 
across 65 destinations, debt-free, with 
cash reserves of around ` 3,400 mn. 
In March 2026, your Board granted in-
principle approval to demerge the Resorts 
and Resort Management business into 
Sterling Holiday Resorts Limited (SHRL). 
The proposed demerger and restructuring 
are being undertaken to unlock value 
for TCIL shareholders and attract 
differentiated investor cohorts for each 
business segment, streamline the existing 
capital structure and enable sharper strategic and operational focus across 
each business vertical, allowing both TCIL 
and SHRL to pursue sector-specific growth 
strategies with agility.

DEI’s revenue. The business responded by 
aligning workforce deployment to demand 
and renegotiating site costs, while adding

Building Trust in a Digital World
As our customer interactions become 
increasingly digital, safeguarding customer 
data remains fundamental to sustaining 
trust. During the year, we advanced a 
comprehensive roadmap to align with the 
Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) 
Act and the accompanying Rules. Through 
an enterprise-wide approach supported 
by robust governance and cross-
functional collaboration, we are embedding 
privacy-by-design across our customer 
touchpoints.
Recognising the increasing scale and 
sophistication of technology-enabled risks, 
we also strengthened our cybersecurity 
capabilities during the year. We enhanced 
our security frameworks, controls and 
monitoring mechanisms and partnered 
with Crowdstrike to further strengthen our 
ability to identify, prevent and respond to 
emerging cyber threats. These measures 
are an integral part of our broader 
commitment to protecting customer information and building resilience across 
our increasingly digital ecosystem.
At the same time, our omnichannel 
model - combining digital platforms 
with more than 300 retail branches, 170-
plus franchise locations and 17 airport 
counters - continues to reaffirm our belief 
that technology is most effective when it 
complements trusted human expertise. 
Our objective has never been to replace 
people with AI, but to equip them with 
better insights and tools, so they can spend 
more time understanding customers and 
delivering personalised travel experiences.
Advancing our Social and 
Environmental Commitments
As we continue to grow, we remain equally 
committed to creating value beyond 
our business. Through the Fairfax India 
Charitable Foundation, we expanded 
access to affordable healthcare and 
strengthened livelihoods in underserved 
communities. Project Dialysis reached 
a significant milestone, supporting 419 
dialysis centres with 1,601 machines 
across 30 states and union territories, 
delivering 3.73 mn cumulative treatment 
sessions and reducing treatment costs for 
patients by an estimated ` 7.4 bn. During 
the year, we further broadened our social 
impact by supporting vocational education 
for tribal students in Nashik and are also 
evaluating how we can expand to support 
more skill development programmes to 
create employment & entrepreneurial 
opportunities.
Our ESG efforts are guided by the 
recognition that the long-term success 
of our businesses is closely linked to the 
sustainability of destinations, ecosystems, 
and communities we serve. Sterling 
advanced its energy efficiency initiatives 
through heat pumps and electric vehicle 
charging infrastructure, while Travel 
Corporation (India) reinforced its climate 
commitments through its Sustainability 
Report and Climate Action Plan. Across our Destination Management 
Services businesses, responsible tourism 
remained a key priority. SITA’s Travelife 
certification, together with Asian Trails’ 
Travelife certification, reflects our 
continued commitment to embedding 
responsible tourism practices across our 
network. Other DMS entities, including 
Private Safaris East Africa and Private 
Safaris South Africa, are progressing 
towards Travelife certification, further 
strengthening our Group-wide 
sustainability journey.
Our initiatives continued to focus on 
responsible tourism, environmental 
conservation and community 
development. These included 
reducing single-use plastics, adopting 
paperless processes, promoting energy 
conservation, expanding conservation-
led tourism initiatives and strengthening 
responsible local partnerships. Alongside 
these efforts, we continued to invest in 
employee well-being and community 
outreach, reinforcing our commitment 
to creating positive outcomes for the 
destinations and communities in which 
we operate.
Our Destination Knowledge Centre 
further advanced this agenda through its 
regenerative tourism framework, which 
seeks to protect natural ecosystems, 
preserve cultural heritage, and create 
long-term socio-economic value for local 
communities.
Together, these efforts reflect our 
commitment to building a responsible 
and sustainable enterprise, creating 
lasting value for our stakeholders while 
contributing positively to the communities 
and environments in which we operate.
Looking Ahead
The world around us will continue to 
evolve. Geopolitical events, technological 
advancements, and changing customer 
expectations will reshape the travel 
industry in ways we cannot fully predict. What gives me confidence is not the hope 
of a stable environment, but the knowledge 
that our organisation has built the agility 
to respond, the discipline to execute, and 
the courage to challenge established ways 
of thinking.
Our focus for the future remains unchanged. 
We will continue to strengthen customer 
trust, deepen our digital capabilities, shape 
distinctive travel experiences, and build 
businesses that create sustainable, long-
term value. Every step we take will be guided 
by a simple belief: lasting resilience comes 
from anticipating change and reinventing 
ourselves ahead of it.
I would like to thank our customers for 
their enduring trust, our employees for their 
passion and commitment, our partners for 
their collaboration, and our shareholders for 
their continued confidence.
In closing, I would like to offer a personal 
reflection. This is my first address as your 
Managing Director, following a leadership 
transition for your Company. I recognise 
the responsibility that comes with this 
role and am committed to building on the 
strong foundations laid over the years, while 
continuing to shape the next chapter of 
Thomas Cook India with ambition, purpose 
and a clear focus on the future.
I am grateful to the Board for its confidence 
and continued trust. I would like to welcome 
Mr. G Mahalingam, who joined the Board 
as an Independent Director and thank Mr. 
Sunil Mathur and Mr. Nilesh Vikamsey, who 
completed their terms during the year for 
their invaluable contribution. 
Above all, I would like to thank our colleagues 
across the Group, whose dedication, 
professionalism, and shared commitment 
continue to drive our progress and position 
us for the future.

Digital Solutions
Scaling through Touchless Operations
Our digital transformation has been a driver of this year's success, driven by 
our focus on creating superior, frictionless, Do-It-Yourself (DIY) customer 
journeys. It has enabled us to deliver faster, simpler and more accessible 
foreign exchange solutions across the customer journey. By integrating mobile 
platforms, conversational commerce, digital onboarding, contactless payments 
and quick-commerce fulfilment, we have created a scalable, touchless 
ecosystem that extends the reach of our services well beyond the traditional 
branch network. These initiatives contributed to digital forex adoption 
increasing to 21.2%.Digital Platforms

Reimagining Forex through Quick Commerce
Recognising the growing preference 
for speed, convenience and digital-first 
experiences, Thomas Cook India became 
the first foreign exchange provider in India 
to partner with Blinkit, introducing forex 
retail as a dedicated quick-commerce 
category. The initiative enables customers 
to order Borderless Travel Cards and Study

complete Video KYC and statutory 
verification digitally, and have their cards 
activated and loaded by Thomas Cook 
India's dedicated forex team.Initially launched across Mumbai, Delhi 
and Bengaluru, the service expanded to

strong customer acceptance and the 
scalability of the model. By combining 
Blinkit's last-mile delivery capabilities 
with Thomas Cook India's digital 
fulfilment ecosystem, the partnership 
strengthens the Company's 
omnichannel strategy while reinforcing 
its position as India's Forex Specialist.

=== page 25 ===
TCPay represents a significant milestone in our digital-first transformation, bringing 
together foreign exchange, prepaid forex cards and international remittances on a single, 
integrated mobile platform. Designed for today’s mobile-first traveller, the application 
enables customers to buy and reload forex cards, purchase and sell foreign currency and 
send international remittances.
The platform combines intelligent navigation with end-to-end digital fulfilment to deliver 
a faster, more intuitive customer experience. Features such as ‘Save for Future Use’ 
functionality, all-in-one card management, real-time card tracking, virtual cards, a multi-
currency wallet, biometric authentication and integrated WhatsApp chat and calling 
simplify transactions while enhancing security and convenience. Customers also benefit 
from personalised in-app offers and promotions, while streamlined workflows have 
reduced transaction completion time by over 30%. Reflecting strong customer adoption, 
app bookings increased 3.5x to 1,722 during the year, reinforcing the growing preference 
for mobile-led foreign exchange services.
Our WhatsApp platform has evolved into a powerful customer engagement channel, 
providing 24x7 access to essential forex services through a simple conversational 
interface. Customers can check balances, download statements, manage PINs and 
card limits, while the introduction of WhatsApp Calling enables direct interaction 
with forex specialists without the need for international calling charges. This digital 
servicing model has significantly improved accessibility and responsiveness, resulting in 
WhatsApp transactions increasing 2.6x to 3,118 during FY 2025-26. Video KYC has transformed the onboarding experience by replacing traditional 
branch-based verification with a secure, paperless and fully digital process. 
Integrated across our online channels, it enables customers to complete 
regulatory verification remotely for forex purchases, prepaid cards and remittance 
services, significantly reducing turnaround times while ensuring full regulatory 
compliance. Combined with doorstep delivery and digital payments, Video KYC 
enables a truly touchless customer journey.
FX Mate continues to strengthen engagement with our partner network by 
simplifying transaction processing and enhancing operational efficiency. The 
platform enables faster execution, improved servicing and greater visibility for 
channel partners, contributing to a more responsive and digitally connected forex 
ecosystem. During FY 2025-26, FX Mate transactions increased 10% to 39,027, 
reflecting sustained partner adoption and higher platform utilisation.
Our website continues to serve as an important digital touchpoint for customers 
seeking convenient access to foreign exchange services. Designed to simplify 
the purchase journey, the platform enables customers to book foreign exchange, 
initiate remittances, complete Video KYC, lock exchange rates and choose 
between doorstep delivery or branch collection through a secure, end-to-end 
digital experience. Reflecting the growing adoption of self-service channels, 
website transactions increased 8% to 4,243 during FY 2025-26.
Our next-generation operating platform for the Foreign Exchange business is 
designed to transform both customer journeys and core operational processes. 
By integrating intelligent automation with digital workflows, the platform has 
significantly enhanced transaction efficiency, streamlined card issuance, 
remittance and payment processing, and strengthened the overall customer 
experience through faster, seamless service delivery. This platform has also 
advanced our transition towards paperless operations, reinforcing operational 
excellence while supporting our broader sustainability objectives.We further strengthened our payments ecosystem by becoming the first forex card 
provider in India to enable contactless cross-border payments through Google Pay in 
partnership with Visa and Mastercard. Customers can securely tokenise and add eligible 
prepaid forex cards to their digital wallets, enabling tap-and-pay transactions across 
millions of NFC-enabled merchant locations worldwide. This innovation enhances both 
payment convenience and transaction security while reducing dependence on physical 
cards during international travel.

Strategic Partnerships A Wide-ranging Network with Omnichannel Reach
Our foreign exchange business is supported by one of India’s most extensive and diversified distribution networks, combining 
owned branches, franchise and agent partners, airport counters, and emerging fulfilment channels. This omnichannel footprint 
enables us to serve customers across key travel touchpoints while ensuring accessibility, convenience and consistent service 
delivery across the country.
During the year, we entered into an exclusive long-term partnership 
with Atlys, one of India’s leading digital visa processing platforms, to 
integrate foreign exchange services directly into the visa application 
process. The collaboration enables travellers to seamlessly access 
Thomas Cook India’s comprehensive forex portfolio, including Borderless 
Travel Card, Study Buddy Card, One Currency Card, foreign currency 
notes and Send Money Abroad services covering 120+ countries, while 
applying for international visas. Supported by digital onboarding, Video 
KYC and secure doorstep delivery, the partnership simplifies travel 
planning by bringing together two essential travel services on a single 
platform, enhancing convenience while strengthening the Company’s 
engagement with digitally savvy leisure and student travellers.Distribution Network
We further enriched our customer proposition through an 
industry-first cross-border rewards programme that extends 
the value of our prepaid forex cards beyond payments. 
Cardholders can enjoy rewards on international spends across 
leading global brands, including Grab, 7-Eleven, Starbucks, 
McDonald’s, KFC, Careem and Burger King, creating a more 
rewarding and differentiated travel experience.
We became the first in India in the cross-border payments category to 
enable contactless payments through Google Pay, in partnership with 
Google Pay and Visa. The initiative enables customers to use their 
Thomas Cook prepaid forex cards for contactless tap-and-pay and online 
transactions using Google Pay while travelling overseas. The offering 
provides a simple, swift, secure and seamless payment experience, with 
global access to transact smoothly and seamlessly across 95 countries.During FY 2025-26, we to refine 
our distribution network, balancing 
expansion into high-growth markets 
with portfolio optimisation. We

including Varanasi, Kottayam,

#2 Travel: B2C Leisure Holidays
The B2C Leisure Holidays vertical stands as a fundamental pillar of the Group’s integrated travel 
ecosystem, operating through an omnichannel framework spanning the Thomas Cook and SOTC 
brands. The portfolio encompasses a comprehensive range of holiday experiences, including 
group inclusive tours (GIT), personalised independent travel (FIT), luxury cruises, charter flight 
operations, and purpose-led pilgrimage circuits.
FY 2025-26 presented a complex operating environment characterised by two principal headwinds. Domestic travel was 
impacted by disruptions across key regions following the Pahalgam attack, while geopolitical tensions in the Middle East 
affected westbound travel, disrupting airline capacity and compressing two of the industry's peak travel seasons.
Against this backdrop, we leveraged the breadth of our portfolio to capture resilient demand across high-growth eastbound 
short-haul markets while further expanding our Spiritual Tourism portfolio. By strategically directing distribution efforts 
towards these high-performing segments, we partly offset volume softness in long-haul destinations, demonstrating the 
strength of our diversified portfolio and market agility.

CASE STUDYOrchestrating Luxury
As one of the first and largest MICE 
movements from India to Mexico, 
this programme brought together 
647 delegates for an experience 
that combined luxury, adventure and 
authentic Mexican culture.
Navigating Complexity at 
Scale
With no direct air connectivity between 
India and Mexico, the movement 
involved multiple flight connections, 
with journey times extending beyond 
36 hours. In view of the prevailing 
geopolitical situation, alternative 
routings were arranged. Transit 
hotels and refreshment facilities were 
provided wherever required to make 
the long journey more comfortable.
Managing an international movement 
of 3,500+ participants to Sri Lanka 
within just 25 days was a significant 
execution challenge, requiring rapid 
planning, cross-functional coordination 
and precise management across travel, 
accommodation, transportation and 
on-ground logistics.
A Pan-India coordination network 
worked closely with destination 
partners to bring multiple workstreams 
together. From managing 10+ 
hotels and participant allocations to June 2025 presented SOTC with an 
unprecedented operational challenge 
when sudden airspace closures and 
airline disruptions impacted two large-
scale international programs.
Approximately 150 delegates were 
stranded in Abu Dhabi for three days, 
100 in London for a similar period, while 
another 55 passengers were stranded at 
Doha Airport for over 12 hours without 
confirmed connectivity to India.
Responding with Agility
Amid the uncertainty, SOTC’s MICE, 
airline and onsite teams remained calm, 
coordinated and focused on one priority: 
the safety and well-being of every 
delegate.The visa process added another 
layer of complexity. Within a strict 
60-day submission window, the team 
managed visa applications for 750 
personnel across Mexico, Turkey, 
Canada and Switzerland, enabling 647 
delegates to travel successfully.
Curating an Experience 
to Remember
The destination experience was 
curated to match the scale and profile 
of the group. Delegates stayed in 
Cancun and experienced highlights 
including the Coco Bongo show, Rio 
Secreto and a premium catamaran 
sailing to Isla Mujeres, with dolphin 
encounters followed by a visit to 
PuntaSur.With prompt client approvals and 
strong DMC support, the team 
arranged three nights of emergency 
accommodation, meals and 
transportation for affected groups in 
Dubai and London.
Behind the scenes, the airline 
team worked tirelessly over three 
consecutive nights to secure 
alternative routings through multiple 
hubs, demonstrating exceptional 
resilience and commitment.
Going beyond the Call of 
Duty
The crisis also brought out the human 
side of our teams.
At Doha, a tour manager provided 
continuous reassurance and personal 
support to anxious passengers despite 
the absence of confirmed seats.
In London, another tour manager went 
above and beyond to support a dealer 
who was diagnosed with chickenpox 
and required an additional 10 days of 
isolation.Managing Luxury MICE 
Operations in Mexico
Turning 25 Days into Seamless ExecutionA Test of Resilience: A Triumph

#2 Travel - B2B DMS
For the Destination Management Specialists (DMS) business, FY 2025-26 tested the value of 
global diversification. Strong growth in India, Africa and Southeast Asia offset regional disruption 
which impacted operations in the Middle East. Spread across many countries, the portfolio held 
its ground through a difficult year. B2B: Destination Management Specialists 
Overview
The DMS business represents the 
most globally diversified of our B2B 
travel businesses. Operating as an 
inbound ground handler across 28 
countries, the business partners with 
overseas tour operators to design 
and run white-labelled, tailored 
travel itineraries for international 
leisure, corporate groups and luxury 
travellers. It is split into two parts, 
India DMS, serving the South Asian 
inbound corridor, and International 
DMS, which spans five continents.
During the fiscal year, the combined 
DMS portfolio recorded a total 
revenue of ` 35,559 mn, up 3% 
y-o-y. The full-year strength of 
the portfolio shows the value of 
spreading across continents, with all 
our international entities delivering

76Sterling Holiday Resorts 
Limited (‘Sterling’) 
continued to strengthen 
its position as one of 
India’s leading leisure 
hospitality companies 
during FY 2025-26. 
Building on the successful

FY 2025-26 marked a defining year for Sterling, a decisive inflection point where scale, profitability and balance sheet 
strength have expanded simultaneously. The hospitality segment delivered a robust performance, driven by higher room 
revenues, improved food and beverage performance and sustained demand across leisure destinations. Revenues from resort 
operations increased by 19% to ` 4,207 mn, supported by a 20% growth in room revenues and a 13% increase in food and 
beverage revenues. Total revenue stood at ` 5,336 mn while EBITDA reached ` 1,753 mn, translating into a healthy margin of 
33%. Earnings Before Tax increased to ` 1,292 mn.
Sterling remained debt free and strengthened its cash reserves to ` 3,395 mn. The consolidated network stood at 78 resorts 
with over 3,810 rooms across owned, leased and managed properties. Sterling reaffirmed the strength of its operating model 
and the sustainability of its growth trajectory.

Way Forward
On March 20, 2026, the Board of Directors of Thomas Cook 
(India) Limited (TCIL) approved The Composite Scheme of 
Arrangement with the objective of unlocking shareholder value, 
enhancing business focus, simplifying the corporate structure 
and optimising the capital structure of TCIL.
As a part of the scheme, the demerger of the resort business into 
Sterling, a company with significant expertise in the hospitality 
sector, is expected to enable focused growth and operational 
efficiencies while facilitating the creation of a dedicated 
hospitality platform. Sterling will be listed on the main board of 
BSE and NSE, upon completion of all regulatory formalities. 
Overall, the Scheme is expected to create long-term value for 
shareholders and other stakeholders.Driving the Next Phase of Growth

Supporting Communities. 
Creating Stronger Futures.
Communities evolve, and so do the ways in which meaningful social value is 
created. Through the Fairfax India Charitable Foundation (FICF), we continue to 
create lasting impact by improving access to quality healthcare while expanding 
opportunities that strengthen education, employability and community resilience.
For nearly a decade, Project Dialysis has remained the cornerstone of our CSR philosophy. As this 
flagship initiative continues to expand its national footprint, FY 2025-26 also marked the beginning 
of a new chapter with the launch of our first vocational education initiative - broadening our impact 
from improving lives to enabling livelihoods.
Project Dialysis
Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) remains 
one of India's most pressing healthcare 
challenges, with an estimated 1 in 7 adults 
at risk and nearly 13 lakh patients requiring 
dialysis. However, limited infrastructure, 
high treatment costs and long travel 
distances continue to restrict access 
to timely treatment, particularly across 
underserved regions. Through Project 
Dialysis, implemented under the Pradhan 
Mantri National Dialysis Programme 
(PMNDP), the Fairfax India Charitable 
Foundation (FICF) addresses this challenge 
by building a collaborative ecosystem that 
delivers free or affordable, quality dialysis 
services closer to where patients live. Today, the programme has evolved into 
one of India's largest corporate-supported 
dialysis initiatives, bringing together 
governments, healthcare providers, 
corporate partners and local communities 
to create a sustainable healthcare 
ecosystem. By combining robust 
governance with technology-enabled 
monitoring and preventive maintenance, 
Project Dialysis continues to deliver 
reliable, quality care while reducing the 
financial and physical burden on patients. Scaling Access. Sustaining Impact.Social Impact ProgressOur Impact Framework
Our approach is designed to create lasting healthcare outcomes by:
 Improving early detection through awareness and community 
outreach 
 Expanding access to quality dialysis in underserved regions 
 Reducing the financial burden of treatment for patients and 
their families 
 Building trained healthcare resources  that strengthen 
local capacity 
The programme is underpinned by four implementation principles - speed of 
programme development, a sustainable ecosystem, meaningful audits and assured 
impact, ensuring every centre consistently delivers reliable, high-quality care.

to develop an additional Skill

Resource efficiency
All our offices across India use LED 
lighting, with workspace design 
focused on maximising natural 
daylight. Air-conditioning systems 
use VRV, VRF and inverter-based 
technologies with environment-
friendly refrigerants. During office 
refurbishments, we are progressively 
introducing materials such as Bharat 
Tiles and low-VOC paints, while 
e-invoicing and digital reporting help 
reduce paper consumption.As most offices operate from shared 
commercial premises, we are 
strengthening the measurement of 
energy and water consumption to 
establish credible baselines and future 
reduction targets.
At our Mumbai corporate office, a 
500 m³ sewage treatment mechanism 
enables wastewater treatment and 
reuse for WC flushing. Flow-restricting 
sprinkler nozzles and bio-based 
cleaning products further support 
water and chemical management. 
Total water consumption declined year 
on year in FY 2025-26, both in absolute 
terms and relative to turnover.
Waste and circularity
Waste is segregated at source across 
our premises and handed over to 
vendors for onward processing in line 
with local guidelines. At our Mumbai 
office, a 200 kg-capacity organic waste converter converts organic waste into 
fertiliser for landscaping, while paper 
waste is recycled into biodegradable 
stationery.
Greener products
Sustainability also extends to our 
product portfolio. The EnterpriseFX 
Card, India's first eco-friendly prepaid 
forex corporate card, is made entirely 
from recycled plastic and features a 
paperless green PIN. For every 25th 
card issued, we plant a tree on behalf 
of the corporate customer, supported 
by e-certification and geo-tagging. 
Each card represents an estimated 
saving of approximately 30 kg of 
carbon emissions.Thomas Cook (India) Limited (TCIL) & SOTC Travel Limited (SOTC)

Re-thinking Water
Our approach to sustainability is 
increasingly reflected in everyday

introduced Impact Water cartons for 
guests, replacing single-use plastic 
water bottles with FSC-certified, 
paper-based cartons that are 
designed to reduce plastic use and 
support more responsible resource 
consumption. The initiative builds 
on our earlier efforts, including the 
introduction of steel water tumblers 
for employees and guests in 2018.
 402,163 plastic water bottles were 
consumed in 2025, highlighting the 
scale of the opportunity to reduce 
single-use plastic. 
 The transition to water cartons 
supports our Climate Action Plan 
commitment to reduce plastic 
consumption by 70% by 2030 and 
has enabled us to reach almost 
100% plastic-free hydration for 
guests, ahead of schedule. 
 The cartons are FSC-certified,  
BPA-free and fully recyclable 
with the cap, with the initiative 
positioned as a practical step 
towards more sustainable 
packaging. 
 The initiative is being rolled out 
across offices, with the distribution 
model also considering lower-
impact transportation, including 
rail where feasible.

Risk Management
We work in a world that is more connected and less predictable, shaped by geopolitical shifts, 
economic swings, changing regulation, new technology and changing traveller preferences. 
These pressures bring real challenges, but they also open room for innovation, diversification 
and sustainable growth, and our job is to be ready for both.
FY 2025-26 reinforced the importance 
of this approach. Geopolitical tensions, 
foreign exchange volatility, weather-
related disruptions and regulatory 
developments tested the resilience of 
the global travel ecosystem. Backed 
by our diversified business portfolio 
spanning Travel and Travel Related 
Services, Foreign Exchange, Hospitality 
and Digital Imaging Solutions across 
28 countries and five continents, 
we remained adaptable, maintained 
business continuity and to create value 
for our stakeholders.
Risk Governance
Risk management is built into our governance framework and strategic decisions. We continuously identify, assess, monitor 
and mitigate enterprise-wide risks through structured policies, robust internal controls and clearly defined accountability 
across the organisation.
Our Enterprise Risk Committee periodically reviews the evolving risk landscape, evaluates mitigation strategies and monitors 
the effectiveness of key controls. Oversight is further strengthened through the Board-level Risk Management Committee, 
which reviews our risk appetite, governance framework and emerging enterprise risks to ensure that risk management remains 
aligned with our long-term strategic priorities.
By embedding resilience into our strategy, operations and decision-making, we continue to strengthen our ability to navigate 
uncertainty, respond to changing market dynamics and create sustainable value for all our stakeholders.Our Key Risks and Mitigation Framework

OVERVIEW:
Global growth is expected to remain moderate and uneven 
amid geopolitical tensions, trade disruptions and tighter 
financial conditions, with energy importers and trade-
exposed economies facing greater pressure, while economies 
integrated into technology value chains benefitting from 
increased AI-related investment. Global trade growth is 
expected to moderate from 5.0% to 3.5% before recovering 
to 4.3% in 2027. Nonetheless, stronger productivity, easing 
trade restrictions and stabilising energy markets could provide 
upside.
India remained one of the fastest-growing major economies in 
FY 2025-26, with real GDP growth accelerating to 7.7% from 
7.1% in FY 2024-25, while real GVA grew by 7.9%. Growth was 
broad-based across agriculture, manufacturing, construction 
and services, supported by strong domestic demand, public 
capital expenditure and infrastructure development. Exports 
of goods and services increased by 9.3%, further supporting 
economic activity. Continued improvements in transport and 
digital connectivity, along with resilient consumption and 
services, strengthened the foundations for sustained growth. 
However, India also faced external pressures from geopolitical 
tensions, disruptions to international routes and supply chains, 
higher energy prices and currency movements. Airspace 
closures across West Asia increased flight distances and 
fuel consumption for long-haul carriers, while domestic fuel 
shortages and higher global crude import costs added pressure 
to transportation and industrial supply chains. Despite these 
challenges, India’s underlying economic fundamentals 
remained supportive.
GOVERNMENT INITIATIVES
Government policy continues to position tourism as a 
key driver of economic growth, employment and regional 
development. The Union Budget 2026-27 focuses on 
destination competitiveness, skills, digitalisation and new 
tourism experiences. India’s airport network has also expanded 
from 74 airports in 2014 to more than 160 in 2025, supported 
by investments in aviation infrastructure and improving rail 
connectivity.
Regional and air connectivity is further expanding access to 
smaller cities and emerging tourist destinations, and, together 
with improved rail and airport infrastructure, are supporting 
the growth of both domestic and international tourism.
Spiritual and experience-led tourism remain important growth 
areas, supported by Swadesh Darshan 2.0 and PRASHAD, 
with a focus on cultural, spiritual, heritage, wellness and rural 
experiences. These initiatives can encourage longer visitor 
stays while creating broader opportunities for accommodation, 
transport, food, handicrafts, retail and local communities.PERFORMANCE OVERVIEW
Thomas Cook India Group recorded a consolidated profit 
after tax of ` 2,204.8 Mn (previous year ` 2,583.9 Mn). This 
Profitability was impacted due to the geopolitical situation 
more pronounced during the last quarter of FY 2025-26.  
Total Income for FY 26 was at ` 85,577.5 Mn as compared 
to ` 82,845.3 Mn in FY 25 reporting a growth of 3.30%.  This 
success can be attributed to the customer centricity, volume 
growth, increased digital initiatives and Company’s strategic 
focus on cost optimization. The Company’s prudent financial 
management  is evident from its strong  position, with cash 
and bank balances held as of March 31, 2026 which stood at  
` 26 Bn.

PROMOTERS
Fairfax Financial Holdings Limited
The Promoter of your Company, Fairbridge Capital (Mauritius) 
Limited (“FCML”) is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Fairfax 
Financial Holdings Limited (“Fairfax”), a company incorporated 
under the laws of Canada and listed on the Toronto Stock 
Exchange.
Fairfax is a holding company which, through its subsidiaries, 
is primarily engaged in property and casualty insurance and 
reinsurance and the associated investment management. 
Fairfax was founded in 1985 by the present Chair and Chief 
Executive Officer, Mr. Prem Watsa. Fairfax has been under 
present management since 1985 and is headquartered in Toronto, Canada. Fairfax’s corporate objective is to achieve 
a high rate of return on invested capital and build long-term 
shareholder value. Since 1985, Fairfax has demonstrated a 
strong financial track record to achieve an annual compounded 
appreciation in book value per share of 18.7% (including 
dividends). As at December 31, 2025, Fairfax has consolidated 
assets of USD 107.8 billion.
Thomas Cook (India) Limited is a part of the Fairfax group. As 
of March 31, 2026, the promoter holds 63.83% of the total paid 
up equity share capital of the Company.

COMPOSITE SCHEME OF ARRANGEMENT
Your Company owns and / or operates multiple resorts across 
India providing retreats in scenic locations amidst natural 
surroundings and hosting curated services across multiple 
attractive market segments. On the other hand, Sterling 
Holiday Resorts Limited  (SHRL) has a wide range of experience 
of running and operating resort business. Your Company and 
SHRL’s Management believes that, the Resort Business of 
your company would reap more benefit from being owned and 
operated by SHRL and that for better focus and maximum 
result it is better to divest the Resort Business into SHRL and 
subsequently list SHRL on the Stock Exchanges. The objective 
is to segregate business verticals, sharpen focus on core 
businesses, and enable both entities to pursue aligned growth 
opportunities, improving efficiency and profitability.
The Management of your company also believes that the 
consolidation of the face value of its equity shares will 
significantly improve key financial ratios, thereby better 
reflecting the true market value of the TCIL’s shares, aligning 
the share price with its intrinsic value and creating financial 
stability and valuation metrics, thereby presenting more accurate representation of the Company’s financial strength 
and long-term prospects.
Furthermore, TC Visa Services (India) Limited, Jardin travels 
Solutions Limited and Borderless Travel Services Limited 
are not engaged in active business operations and continue 
to incur routine compliance and administrative cost.  Their 
absorption into TCIL will streamline the corporate structure 
and reduce overheads, resulting in increased efficiency and 
focus on core business activities.
The Management of your company is of the view that 
reduction of share capital of TCIL is necessary to right size the 
balance sheet and have an efficient capital structure and that 
the shareholders also benefit in terms of improved earnings 
per share. The proposed reduction of the equity share capital 
of TCIL would not have any adverse effect on the creditors of 
TCIL or on the Company’s ability to meet its obligations in the 
ordinary course of business as there is no payout resulting 
from the proposed capital reduction.
Accordingly, the Board of Directors of your  Company at its 
meeting held on March 20, 2026, approved the Composite 
Scheme of Arrangement amongst Thomas Cook (India) Limited 
(“Demerged Company” or “Transferee Company” or “TCIL”) 
and Sterling Holiday Resorts Limited (“Resulting Company” 
or “SHRL”) and TC Visa Services (India) Limited (“Transferor 
Company 1” or “TCVSL”) and Jardin Travel Solutions Limited 
(“Transferor Company 2” or “JTSL”) and Borderless Travel 
Services Limited (“Transferor Company 3” or “BTSL”) and their 
respective shareholders. The Scheme inter-alia  provided:
a) The demerger of the Demerged Undertaking of TCIL into 
SHRL as a going concern with effect from the Appointed 
Date, and issuance and allotment of New Shares by 
the Resulting Company i.e. SHRL to all the Eligible 
Shareholders of TCIL as per the Share Entitlement Ratio 
in the manner set out in this Scheme;
b) The consolidation of 4 (four) equity shares of TCIL of face 
value of ` 1/- (Indian Rupee One Only) each into 1 (one) 
equity share of TCIL of face value of ` 4/- (Indian Rupees 
Four Only) each, in the manner set out in this Scheme;
c) The amalgamation of TCVSL, JTSL and BTSL with TCIL 
in the manner set out in this Scheme and consequent 
dissolution of TCVSL, JTSL and BTSL without being 
wound up; and
d) Reduction of paid-up equity share capital of TCIL by 
reducing the face value of paid-up equity shares from ` 4/- 
(Indian Rupees Four Only) per equity share to ` 3/- (Indian 
Rupees Three Only) per equity share in the manner set out 
in this Scheme.
The said Composite Scheme of Arrangement is subject to 
requisite statutory and regulatory approvals and sanction by 
the respective shareholders of each of the Companies involved 
in the Scheme.

INVESTOR EDUCATION AND PROTECTION FUND (IEPF) 
AWARENESS INITIATIVE – SAKSHAM NIVESHAK CAMPAIGN
The Investor Education and Protection Fund Authority (IEPFA), 
Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA), launched the Campaign, 
titled  “Saksham Niveshak”,  aimed at facilitating shareholders 
whose dividends remain unpaid or unclaimed, with a special 
focus on KYC updation and compliance with prescribed 
regulatory requirements.
Your Company has consistently undertaken various initiatives 
to assist shareholders in claiming their unpaid/unclaimed 
dividends and updating their records. As part of its ongoing 
shareholder outreach efforts, the Company has been 
periodically communicating with concerned shareholders 
through reminder letters and other modes of communication, 
encouraging them to update their KYC details and claim their 
pending entitlements.
In line with the aforesaid initiative of the IEPFA, the Company 
participated in the “Saksham Niveshak” 100-Days awareness 
campaign contemplated by the IEPF authorities and continued 
its efforts to create awareness among shareholders regarding 
unpaid/unclaimed dividends, KYC updation, nomination 
requirements, and other related compliance measures, with 
the objective of facilitating the claim process and enhancing 
shareholder services. The Company initiated a 100 Days

Hundred Thousand) ordinary shares of EUR 1 (One Euro)

commenced its business operations.
• The Board of Directors at its meeting held on November

addendum to the Share Subscription cum Joint Venture 
Agreement (JVA) dated September 30, 2024 with Atirath 
Technologies Private Limited (“JV Partner”) and Indian 
Horizon Marketing Services Limited (“JV Co.”), further

Joint Venture Agreement (‘Supplemental Agreement’)

co - developing the Travel AI Platform. Furthermore, the 
Sub-Committee of Board of Directors on March 27, 2026 
authorised the subscription by way of Preferential Offer of 
25,00,000 Class A Equity Shares of ` 10/- each of the JV co.
• Travel Circle International (Mauritius) Limited, a 
subsidiary of the Company in Mauritius, on October 29, 
2025 intimated to the Company about a change in the 
shareholding structure of one of its step-down subsidiaries 
i.e Desert Adventures Tourism Company, Jordan (DATC). 
Desert Adventures Tourism LLC (Dubai) (DAT LLC) a 
subsidiary of Travel Circle International (Mauritius) 
Limited was already exercising 100% control over DATC 
through 50% direct stake and 50% beneficial stake 
through a nominee shareholder, in accordance with the 
then prevailing Jordanian Law. With the relaxation in local 
Jordanian law, allowing 100% foreign shareholding, the 
Desert Adventures Tourism LLC entity felt it appropriate 
to become the 100% direct stakeholder. Accordingly, the 
local Jordanian nominee shareholder has transferred 50% 
of the shares held by him to Desert Adventures Tourism 
LLC (Dubai) (the Beneficial Owner), which results in the 
DAT LLC holding 100% of the share capital .

ANNUAL REPORT ON CORPORATE SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY 
(CSR) ACTIVITIES FOR FY 2025-26
1. BRIEF OUTLINE ON CSR POLICY OF THE COMPANY:
 CSR vision:
 Thomas Cook (India) Limited exists not only for doing good business, but equally to do good for society.
 As a result of this holistic vision, aimed at achieving long-term stakeholder value creation, the Company seamlessly integrates  
its CSR efforts with its pursuit of business excellence in a mutually beneficial manner.
 Thomas Cook (India) Limited shall always continue to respect the interests of and be responsive towards the communities it 
serves and operates in especially those from socially and economically backward groups, the underprivileged and marginalized; 
thereby, society at large.
 “As an integral part of our commitment to Good Corporate Citizenship, we at Thomas Cook (India) Limited will actively work to 
improve the quality of life of the  people in the communities we serve. We shall relentlessly strive  to partner with the Government, 
respected socially conscious agencies and NGOs in the noble efforts of nation-building via sustainable economic & social 
development, inclusive growth and social equity”.
 CSR Charter & Focus:
 In our CSR journey, we shall selectively deploy our financial resources earmarked for CSR to drive an action agenda in line 
with Schedule VII of the Companies Act, 2013 as recommended by the CSR Committee of the Company and overseen by the 
Management and nominated representatives from the Board of Directors.
 The Company’s annual CSR budget and efforts shall focus on:
1. Health  and Sanitation:
 Improving access to healthcare by focusing on developing a high impact, holistic, sustainable and collaborative ecosystem 
that offers free/ affordable, quality healthcare services to underprivileged population in parts of India where there is limited 
healthcare infrastructure/ access including undertaking Project Dialysis through Fairfax India Charitable Foundation 
(Implementing Agency)  by collaborating with government on a public private partnership supporting Pradhan Mantri 
National Dialysis Program (PMNDP) or supporting private charitable organization  thereby developing access to dialysis at 
parts of India where  there is poor dialysis infrastructure.
 The locations where the Company has setup Dialysis Centre are mentioned in Annexure A herein below.
 Addressing lack of hygiene and sanitation facilities at tourist spots Pan India or on highways enroute to these tourist spots. 
This will be done by setting up/managing environment friendly toilet facilities and the underprivileged local population will 
be trained in the upkeep of  these facilities.
2. Any other Project or Programme that falls under  the purview of Schedule VII of Section 135 of the  Companies Act, 2013, 
as identified and approved from time to time.

SECTION B: MANAGEMENT AND PROCESS DISCLOSURES
This section describes the structures, policies and processes aligned to nine principles of business responsibility. These briefly 
are as follows:
P1: Businesses should conduct and govern themselves with Ethics, Transparency and Accountability 
P2: Businesses should provide goods and services in a manner that is sustainable and safe
P3: Businesses should respect and promote the well-being of all employees, including those in their value chains 
P4: Businesses should respect the interests of and be responsive to all its stakeholders
P5: Businesses should respect and promote human rights
P6: Businesses should respect and make efforts to protect and restore the environment
P7: Businesses, when engaged in influencing public and regulatory policy, should do so in a manner that is responsible and transparent
P8: Businesses should promote inclusive growth and equitable development
P9: Businesses should engage with and provide value to their consumers in a responsible manner

10. Health and safety management system
a. Whether an occupational health and safety management system has been implemented by the entity?
 Yes, the organization emphasizes the importance of maintaining a safe and healthy workplace for all employees, workers 
and third-party stakeholders who work on its premises.
1 We have annual maintenance contract for all critical and noncritical equipment’s wherein regular planned maintenance 
activities are conducted for enhancement of life and to avoid any breakdowns/hazards of equipment’s.
2 Fire Drills
3 Access Control System
4 Fire Detection System & Fire Fighting System.
5 CCTV Monitoring
6	 We	conduct	structural	audits	of	the	office	infrastructures	wherever	required.
7 We conduct Food quality testing.
8	 Branch	visits	are	done	to	make	sure	that	office	is	being	maintained	properly.
9 Health awareness campaigns and employee medical camps
b. What are the processes used to identify work-related hazards and assess risks on a routine and non-routine basis by 
the entity?
1	 Hazardous	areas	like	electrical	panels,	pumps,	Fire	Pumps	etc.	are	identified	and	signages	are	displayed.
2 Access is provided to authorize people only at critical areas like server room, electrical rooms etc.
=== page 89 ===
172
3 Safety PPE kits are encouraged to electrical staffs during the maintenance or operation work.
4 Fire Exit Signages are displayed at all appropriate locations.
5	 Relevant	 Fire	Extinguishers	 are	placed	across	the	office	and	critical	areas	such	as	server	room/Hub	 room,	Electrical	
panels, cafeteria kitchen etc.
c. Whether you have processes for workers to report the work related hazards and to remove themselves from such risks
 Yes
d. Do the employees/ worker of the entity have access to non-occupational medical and healthcare services?
 Yes. Thomas Cook (India) Limited recognizes that overall wellbeing of its employees is integral to its success and growth 
aspirations. Employees are covered under group medical insurance where in non-occupational medical and healthcare 
services are availed from ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company Limited. Contractual employees are registered in ESIC 
and some contract staffs are also covered under Mediclaim insurance.
 The Company also takes a CGL global insurance policy to cover any 3rd party claims arising due to injuries during work 
in	our	offices.	Primary	necessities	 like	First	Aid	box,	sick	bay,	wheel	chairs,	stretcher	 and	basic	medical	supplies	for	
emergencies	are	available	across	all	offices.

Global Economic Overview
The global economy in CY 2026 continues to demonstrate 
resilience amid evolving geopolitical developments, with steady 
activity across major regions supported by ongoing adaptation 
in energy markets, trade routes, and global supply chains. While 
the conflict in the Middle East has influenced energy markets, 
transportation networks and supply chains, economies have 
continued to adjust through diversified sourcing and rerouted 
trade flows. Against this backdrop, global growth is projected 
at 3.0% in CY 2026, before recovering to 3.4% in CY 2027.
